findings.rule: Title block heat treatment must not contradict or omit referenced process notes.
findings.reasoning: The title-block heat_treatment field is '---' (none), yet note N1 explicitly requires case hardening to 55–60 HRC with a 0.8–2 mm case depth. A manufacturer reading only the title block would skip heat treatment entirely, producing a soft part that fails in service.
findings.correction: Update the title-block heat_treatment field to reference N1 (e.g., 'CASE HARDEN 55-60 HRC PER NOTE N1') so the requirement is unambiguous.

findings.rule: Functional bore diameters on a sleeve must carry a tolerance or fit class.
findings.reasoning: Dimensions D3 (⌀12) and D4/D12 (⌀20) define the inner bores of a pin sleeve. With no explicit tolerance they fall back to the general machining tolerance of ±0.5 mm (for sizes 6–30 mm per the table), which is far too loose for any functional pin-fit purpose.
findings.correction: Assign an appropriate fit-class tolerance (e.g., H7 or a specific ± limit) to the functional bore diameters D3 and D4/D12.

findings.rule: Functional outer diameters on a sleeve must carry a tolerance or fit class.
findings.reasoning: Dimensions D1 and D13 (⌀30) define the outer cylindrical surface of the sleeve. Without an explicit tolerance they default to ±0.5 mm under the general machining tolerances, which is unacceptable if this OD mates with a housing or bearing seat.
findings.correction: Add a suitable tolerance or fit class (e.g., h6, h7, or explicit limits) to the outer diameter dimensions D1 and D13.

findings.rule: Threads running into a shoulder require relief or an undercut unless kept short intentionally.
findings.reasoning: Feature F4 describes an M5 × 6 deep threaded hole. If this thread terminates at a shoulder inside the blind hole, standard taps cannot produce full-depth threads without a relief groove or undercut. Note N1 item 3 ('THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT') implies the threads exist before hardening, but does not address bottom-of-hole geometry.
findings.correction: Confirm whether the M5 hole bottoms against a shoulder; if so, add a thread-relief undercut or reduce the specified thread depth to leave adequate tap clearance.
